page.title: A clearer view of your days.
page.description: Explore Vietnamese lunar dates, remember special occasions and make time for what matters.
page.seoDescription: Vietnamese solar and lunar calendar, holidays and a time-off calculator. Available in Vietnamese, English, Traditional and Simplified Chinese.

footer.madeFor: A little perspective on your days.

newYear.name: New Year's Day
newYear.description: The first day of the Gregorian year.

tet.name: Vietnamese Lunar New Year
tet.description: The first day of the first lunar month. The full Tết break is announced separately each year and by each workplace.

firstFullMoon.name: First Full Moon Festival
firstFullMoon.description: The fifteenth day of the first lunar month, known in Vietnam as Tết Nguyên tiêu.

hungKings.name: Hùng Kings Commemoration
hungKings.description: The tenth day of the third lunar month, commemorating the Hùng Kings.

doanNgo.name: Tết Đoan Ngọ
doanNgo.description: The fifth day of the fifth lunar month, a traditional Vietnamese festival.

vuLan.name: Vu Lan Festival
vuLan.description: The fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month, an occasion to honour parents.

nationalDay.name: Vietnam National Day
nationalDay.description: September 2. The adjoining day off and any workday swaps follow annual announcements.

midAutumn.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
midAutumn.description: The fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month, a time for family reunions and children's celebrations.

kitchenGods.name: Kitchen Gods' Day
kitchenGods.description: The twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month, marking preparations for the new year.

womensDay.name: International Women's Day
womensDay.description: March 8. An observance, not automatically a day off.

vietnameseWomensDay.name: Vietnamese Women's Day
vietnameseWomensDay.description: October 20. An observance, not automatically a day off.

teachersDay.name: Vietnamese Teachers' Day
teachersDay.description: November 20, an occasion to thank teachers.

vietnamCultureDay.name: Vietnam Culture Day
vietnamCultureDay.description: November 24. Since 2026, workers have been entitled to one day off with full pay.

remembranceDay.name: War Invalids and Martyrs Day
remembranceDay.description: July 27 honours those who served and sacrificed for Vietnam. It is a paid public holiday from 2027.

partyFounding.name: Founding of the Communist Party of Vietnam
partyFounding.description: Marks the founding of the Communist Party of Vietnam on 3 February 1930.

physiciansDay.name: Vietnamese Doctors’ Day
physiciansDay.description: Observed on 27 February to honor people who work in healthcare.

coldFoodFestival.name: Vietnamese Cold Food Festival
coldFoodFestival.description: On the third day of the third lunar month, many families offer rice dumplings to their ancestors.

buddhaBirthday.name: Buddha’s Birthday
buddhaBirthday.description: On the full moon of the fourth lunar month, Buddhists commemorate the birth of Shakyamuni Buddha.

hoChiMinhBirthday.name: Ho Chi Minh’s Birthday
hoChiMinhBirthday.description: Commemorates the birth of President Ho Chi Minh on 19 May 1890.

childrensDay.name: International Children’s Day
childrensDay.description: Observed in Vietnam on 1 June to celebrate children and recognize their rights.

revolutionaryPressDay.name: Vietnam Revolutionary Press Day
revolutionaryPressDay.description: Marks the publication of the first issue of Thanh Niên on 21 June 1925.

familyDay.name: Vietnamese Family Day
familyDay.description: Observed annually on 28 June to celebrate Vietnamese families.

augustRevolution.name: August Revolution Day
augustRevolution.description: Marks the success of the August Revolution uprising in Hanoi on 19 August 1945.

doubleNinth.name: Double Ninth Festival
doubleNinth.description: A traditional festival on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month.

doubleTenth.name: Tết Thường Tân
doubleTenth.description: A traditional Vietnamese festival on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month, also called Tết Trùng thập.

haNguyen.name: Tết Hạ Nguyên
haNguyen.description: On the full moon of the tenth lunar month, some Vietnamese communities give thanks after the harvest with offerings of newly harvested rice.

vietnamLawDay.name: Vietnam Law Day
vietnamLawDay.description: Observed on 9 November, the date Vietnam adopted its first Constitution in 1946.

nationalUnityDay.name: National Great Unity Festival
nationalUnityDay.description: Observed on 18 November, the traditional anniversary of the Vietnam Fatherland Front.

vietnamHeritageDay.name: Vietnam Cultural Heritage Day
vietnamHeritageDay.description: Observed on 23 November to celebrate and preserve Vietnam’s cultural heritage.

vietnamRedCrossAnniversary.name: Vietnam Red Cross Founding Anniversary
vietnamRedCrossAnniversary.description: Marks the founding of the organization that became the Vietnam Red Cross Society on 23 November 1946.

peoplesArmyDay.name: Vietnam People’s Army Founding Day
peoplesArmyDay.description: Observed on 22 December, which is also All-People’s National Defense Day in Vietnam.

christmas.name: Christmas Day
christmas.description: December 25. Not automatically a day off in Vietnam.
